title: Guacamole
subtitle: Fresh avocado dip with lime, coriander, and jalapeño
excerpt: Guacamole is a Mexican avocado dip made from mashed ripe avocado, lime juice, coriander, onion, and jalapeño. It takes 10 minutes and requires ripe avocados above all else. The best guacamole is chunky, not smooth, with bright lime acidity and fresh herb flavour.
sourceNotes: Guacamole is derived from the Nahuatl word ahuacamolli (avocado sauce). The Aztec preparation of mashed avocado with tomato and chilli was noted by Spanish conquistadors in the 16th century. The modern version is defined by avocado, lime, and coriander and is eaten throughout Mexico and the Mexican diaspora.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make within 30 minutes of serving. Press cling film directly onto the surface to slow browning.

content.text: Ripe avocados are the only thing that matters. Press the avocado gently: it should yield slightly to pressure but not feel mushy. Bright green, firm avocados will not ripen properly at home in time. Plan ahead. The lime juice brightens the flavour and slows browning. Mash with a fork, not a blender: blenders make it too smooth.

items.prepNote: finely chopped, seeds removed for less heat
white or red onion, very finely chopped

content.text: Scoop the avocado flesh into a bowl. Add the lime juice immediately and season with salt. Mash with a fork to your preferred texture: some cooks prefer completely smooth, most prefer chunky with visible pieces.
Add the coriander, jalapeño, and onion. Stir to combine. Add the diced tomato if using. Taste and adjust: more lime if it needs brightness, more salt, more jalapeño if you want heat.

items.cause: Too little lime juice, or left uncovered
items.fix: Add more lime juice. Press cling film directly onto the surface of the guacamole to exclude air. The avocado stone placed in the bowl is a myth; it only protects the surface directly under it.
